Excavation Headlines: Evidence or Exaggeration?

A 90-minute discussion, online or at your campus

Made for your group

  • Your day and start time, weekends and special days included
  • Any group size, from one person to a whole class
  • Your pace and your language: English, Hindi or both

Arranged for your group. Send your preferred dates, group size and location. We adapt the length, level and language, and prepare a quotation. The suggested group size is a guide, not a requirement.

Request on WhatsApp Request by email

No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

In this discussion you learn to evaluate archaeological news claims and scientific limitations.

It is run as a guided conversation, online or on your campus, and works best with a group that is ready to argue a point.

What it covers

  • Headline comparison
  • How excavation reports work
  • Group evidence scoring
  • Take-home verification framework

How the time is spent

  1. Headline comparison 15 min

  2. How excavation reports work 25 min

  3. Group evidence scoring 30 min

  4. Take-home verification framework 20 min

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Compare news headlines about excavations with the evidence behind them.
  • Explain how excavation reports work and what scientific limitations apply to them.
  • Score archaeological news claims against the evidence using a verification framework.

You take away

An interpretation sheet with questions to ask on site and suggested reading.
